literal_effects: Memory forms store the independently seeded source XMM low 128 bits to the actual 16-byte destination without changing vector state. Register forms copy those 128 bits to the r/m destination and zero destination bits 511:128. Full GPR, flags, selectors, FP, stack, data and source comparisons remain; only the declared destination may change.
negative_endpoint: Eight original-PC failed 16-byte writes cover full no-access/read-only, both crossing protection directions, read-only stack, and base/RIP source destinations. Each retains exit 125, zero TRACE and no store completion. Complete native/TF before and post memory images must agree; outside the potential range bytes stay unchanged, and inside each byte remains old or equals its corresponding source byte. No store atomicity is assumed; source-write controls additionally require complete original source equality.
